classification.difficultyReason: Apply two specified axis reflections in sequence, track intermediate and final coordinates, and recognise that a point on the first axis stays fixed.

content.prompt: Mark the given points on a number plane. Find their images when they are first reflected in the $x$-axis and then in the $y$-axis. Label the axes and image points, and give the coordinates of the images.

answer.worked:
Across the $x$-axis, place $A'$ 1 unit above the axis, keeping $x=2$. Across the $y$-axis, place $A''$ 2 units to the left, keeping $y=1$.

$$\begin{aligned}A'&=(2,1)\\A''&=(-2,1)\end{aligned}$$

Across the $x$-axis, place $B'$ 2 units below the axis, keeping $x=2$. Across the $y$-axis, place $B''$ 2 units to the left, keeping $y=-2$.

$$\begin{aligned}B'&=(2,-2)\\B''&=(-2,-2)\end{aligned}$$

Across the $x$-axis, place $C'$ 3 units below the axis, keeping $x=-3$. Across the $y$-axis, place $C''$ 3 units to the right, keeping $y=-3$.

$$\begin{aligned}C'&=(-3,-3)\\C''&=(3,-3)\end{aligned}$$

$D$ lies on the $x$-axis, so the first reflection leaves it fixed. Across the $y$-axis, place $D''$ 5 units to the right, keeping $y=0$.

$$\begin{aligned}D'&=(-5,0)\\D''&=(5,0)\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Complete shared solution plane showing all original points and both successive images. Coincident D and D′ have one combined label.
spec.mathematics: First reflect across the x-axis, preserving horizontal distance and reversing vertical position; then reflect across the y-axis, preserving vertical position and reversing horizontal position.
